title: Preflight & Sentinel Evals for Catalog and Tenant Pin Migrations
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: Catalog and customer-pinned model upgrades are a frequent vector for silent quality regressions. Operators often discover degradations only after rollouts are complete and customers report issues. We need an automated preflight + sentinel evaluation orchestration that runs whenever a model version is pinned or upgraded in either the public catalog or a tenant's locked model.

Goal: Provide a lightweight, tenant-aware, cost-controlled evaluation pipeline that: (1) runs preflight synthetic probes targeted to the changed behaviors in the model/config delta, (2) flags regressions based on configurable thresholds, (3) surfaces clear pass/fail signals with rollback recommendations, and (4) integrates with rollout policies (canary, staged, auto-rollback). This ticket captures the PM scope and acceptance criteria; engineering tickets will break out the orchestration, sampling, and cost-throttle work.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Define orchestration rules and signal thresholds for preflight/sentinel evals triggered by pin/upgrade events for catalog and tenant locks.
- Tenant-aware sampling policy (priority tiers, traffic footprint, and sample budgets).
- Cost throttles and governor to bound eval compute spend per tenant and per catalog change.
- Signal definition: delta metrics (accuracy-like task metrics, hallucination rate proxies, token-efficiency regressions), aggregated confidence, and severity scoring.
- Integration points: event source (pin-change webhook), eval runner API, results webhook to Console, and automatic rollback recommendation to rollout service.
- UX text and Console telemetry hooks so on-call and customers can understand why a pin was blocked or rolled back.

Out of scope: building new heavy fidelity eval frameworks (we will reuse existing synthetic probes and the probe sampler), deep semantic eval model training, and long-running tenant-specific test suites (those are follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: When a catalog or tenant pin is created/updated, the pin-change service emits an event and the preflight orchestration schedules an eval job within 2 minutes.
Eval runner runs a prioritized set of 50-200 synthetic probes (configurable by tenant priority) and returns a scored delta compared to the pinned baseline.

System computes an overall severity score and marks the pin as PASS/REVIEW/FAIL using thresholds defined in the policy table; PASS allows rollout, FAIL triggers automatic hold and a rollback recommendation in the rollout UI.

Cost throttle prevents spending more than X GPU-minutes per tenant per pin event (configurable; default 60 GPU-min), with circuit-breaker behavior that demotes sample size rather than failing the preflight by default.
Console UI surfaces the top 5 probe failures, delta metrics, and a link to the detailed eval run within the pin/change page.
Integration tests exist that simulate catalog and tenant pin events and assert correct lifecycle (event -> run -> score -> flag) in staging.
Monitoring: a dashboard shows preflight-run rate, mean time to completion, false-positive rate (sampling vs historical), and cost burn by tenant for the last 30 days.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive sampling gives higher fidelity but increases cost and longer preflight latency. We will default to an adaptive policy that prefers targeted probes and expands only if initial signals are marginal.
Open question: Should 'critical' enterprise tenants be allowed a higher default sample budget? Proposal: honor tenant tier with a capped multiplier (1x for self-serve, 3x for enterprise).
We must ensure tenant privacy: sandbox evals must not leak customer data; preflight runs should use synthetic inputs or tenant-provided anonymized fixtures.
We will reuse the existing probe catalog and add a metadata flag for 'suitable-for-preflight' probes.

2025-02-18 - Jordan Patel: Reviewed scope; engineering alignment required on compute budget enforcement and API surface for scheduling. Asked ENG to estimate orchestration work (see ENG-42177).

2025-02-22 - Priya Nair (Engineering): Raised concern about blocking rollouts when eval backlog forms during heavy catalog activity. Suggested a degraded mode: allow rollouts with stricter monitoring, tag rollout as 'partial-guarded' if preflight queue exceeds threshold.

2025-02-26 - Maya Li (Design): Sent wireframes for Console treatment of preflight results and suggested a concise summary card with top failure reasons and a one-click rollback action. Link: https://confluence.redwood/example/preflight-ui
